To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

P19 embryonal carcinoma cells exposed to retino ic acid and plated onto cultured mouse cortical glia differentiated into neuron-like cells exhibiting glutamate receptor mediated currents and toxicity.
P19 cells differentiated into neuronal cells with functional NMDA and non-NMDA receptor subtypes and that these cells were susceptible to glutamate receptor-mediated toxicity.

P19 cells, when treated with retinoic acid, differentiate into cells that are immunopositive for neurofilament and neuron-specific eno-lase, exhibit inward currents in response both to NMDA and kainate, and undergo death following exposure to excitatory amino acids.

the development of cell lines which exhibit excitotoxicity and glutamate receptor-mediated responses, and the use of these cell lines to investigate the molecular basis of excitotoxicity.
the development of a cell line exhibiting glutamate receptor responses and toxicity.
the role of excitotoxicity in neurodegenerative diseases, and the mechanisms underlying excitotoxic cell death.

the P19 cells exhibit both excitatory amino-acid responses and vulnerability to glutamate toxicity, which are characteristics of neurons in the central nervous system.
